note: Machine-readable digest of docs/notes/resource-library.md. One entry per source. category maps to the site sectors: frontend, data-bridge, backend-sector, database-void, ux-lab, delivery-deck, meta, plus two decks added 2026-09-10 — interview (hiring preparation) and humanities (historical, philosophical and beletristic reading, off the critical path). access tells how a resource is reached: free (no payment), subscription (paid platform like Everand/Scribd), purchase (fixed price per book), borrow (Archive.org temporary lending).

sources.title: Intro to HTML/CSS
sources.annotation: The ship's current pace-setting HTML course.

sources.title: HTML & CSS: Design and Build Websites
sources.annotation: Classic beginner book; on Scribd/Everand subscription.

sources.title: Learn JavaScript — Full Course for Beginners
ng-book: The Complete Book on Angular
Foundations of UX Design (Google UX Cert)
Eloquent JavaScript (4th ed.)
sources.annotation: The language book for the backend route too.

sources.title: High Performance Browser Networking
sources.annotation: Ilya Grigorik; free on the author's site.

sources.title: Documenting APIs — I'd Rather Be Writing
CS50 SQL — Introduction to Databases with SQL
30 Days of SQL — from Basic to Advanced
SQL Full Course for Beginners — 30 Hours (Data with Baraa)
sources.annotation: Free 30 h zero-to-hero video course with visual animations.

sources.title: SQL QuickStart Guide — Walter Shields
sources.annotation: Simplified beginner's guide to managing, analyzing, and manipulating data with SQL; ClydeBank Media.

sources.title: Practical SQL, 2nd Edition — Anthony DeBarros
sources.annotation: Beginner's guide to storytelling with data, built on PostgreSQL; No Starch Press.

sources.title: SQL in 10 Minutes a Day, 5th Edition — Ben Forta
sources.annotation: Best-selling quick lessons that cover the SQL you actually need; Sams/Pearson.

sources.title: Big Data: A Very Short Introduction — Dawn Holmes
sources.annotation: OUP VSI; what big data is, why it matters, and how it changed what databases are for.

sources.title: Seven Databases in Seven Weeks, 2nd Edition — Luc Perkins, Jim Wilson, Eric Redmond
sources.annotation: Guided tour across PostgreSQL, Redis, Neo4j, Cassandra, etc.; teaches the shape of the database landscape; ISBN 9781680502534.

sources.title: An Introduction to Database Systems — C. J. Date
sources.annotation: The classic on the relational model — the foundation the whole SQL world builds on; 8th ed., free borrow on Archive.org.

sources.title: Database Design for Mere Mortals, 2nd Edition — Michael J. Hernandez
sources.annotation: The practical design book: tables, keys, relationships, business rules, normalization — free borrow on Archive.org.

sources.title: Introduction of ER Model (GeeksforGeeks)
sources.annotation: Free first-step data-modeling primer: entities, attributes, relationships, ER diagrams.

sources.title: Let's Build a Simple Database (cstack)
sources.annotation: Builds a sqlite clone from scratch in C in 15 parts — the 'how a database actually works' missing context.

sources.title: Redis University — Get Started with Redis
RFC 8259 — The JSON Data Interchange Format
Git and GitHub for Beginners — Crash Course
Learn Git — Full Course for Beginners
Introduction to GitHub
sources.annotation: Your first day in under an hour.

sources.title: roadmap.sh
sources.annotation: Community roadmaps to choose the next course.

sources.title: Teach Yourself Programming in Ten Years
The TypeScript Handbook
sources.annotation: The official reference. Types are documentation the compiler can check.

sources.title: Beginner's TypeScript (tutorial)
sources.annotation: Matt Pocock. Free tier is enough for Phase 3; do not buy before finishing it.

sources.title: TypeScript Deep Dive
sources.annotation: Basarat Ali Syed. Free online, for when the Handbook runs short.

sources.title: Type Challenges
sources.annotation: Puzzles for the type system. Drill, not spine.

sources.title: Package management basics (npm)
sources.annotation: What npm actually does, before the first React project needs it.

sources.title: Vite — Getting Started
sources.annotation: The build tool that turns .ts into something a browser can run.

sources.title: Testing Library — docs & guiding principles
sources.annotation: Test what the user sees, not what the component stores.

sources.title: Playwright — Getting Started
sources.annotation: End-to-end tests in a real browser. Required for the green-CI gate.

sources.title: What are browser developer tools?
sources.annotation: The highest-leverage daily skill, and the one nobody teaches deliberately.

sources.title: Chrome DevTools documentation
sources.annotation: Inspect, breakpoint, profile. Learn it early, not when desperate.

sources.title: Tech Interview Handbook
sources.annotation: Opens week 24, when applications begin — not at the end.

sources.title: GreatFrontEnd — practice questions
sources.annotation: Free tier is substantial; paid tier optional.

sources.title: Exercism — JavaScript track
sources.annotation: Free human mentoring on submitted solutions. Rare and valuable.

sources.title: Sketch of the Analytical Engine — with Ada Lovelace's Notes
sources.annotation: Menabrea 1843, translated and annotated by Lovelace. Her Notes are longer than the text they annotate — the first programmer was also the first commentator.

sources.title: The Thrilling Adventures of Lovelace and Babbage
sources.annotation: Sydney Padua. Meticulously footnoted historical comedy. The webcomic is free.

sources.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (1950)
sources.annotation: Turing. Reads as philosophy of mind, because it is.

sources.title: As We May Think (1945)
sources.annotation: Vannevar Bush imagines the hyperlink, decades early.

sources.title: The Victorian Internet
sources.annotation: Tom Standage. The telegraph as the first internet, with the same moral panics.

sources.title: Weaving the Web
sources.annotation: Berners-Lee on why the web was given away rather than sold.

sources.title: Programming as Theory Building (1985)
sources.annotation: Peter Naur. Programming is theory-building, not text-production. Twelve pages that reframe the whole craft — start here.

sources.title: Literate Programming (1984)
sources.annotation: Knuth: write programs for humans to read. The direct ancestor of this project's @tag doctrine.

sources.title: The Humble Programmer (EWD340, 1972)
sources.annotation: Dijkstra's Turing Award lecture. Aphoristic and superbly bad-tempered.

sources.title: The Rise of "Worse is Better"
sources.annotation: Richard Gabriel on why the uglier design keeps winning.

sources.title: The Mythical Man-Month
sources.annotation: Brooks, 1975. Adding people to a late project makes it later. Still true.

sources.title: Tools for Conviviality
sources.annotation: Ivan Illich. Philosophy proper — when does a tool stop serving its user?

sources.title: Close to the Machine
sources.annotation: Ellen Ullman. A programmer's memoir, and genuinely literary.

sources.title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
sources.annotation: Hofstadter on recursion and self-reference — this project's own central metaphor.

sources.title: The Soul of a New Machine
sources.annotation: Tracy Kidder. Pulitzer-winning. Engineering as narrative nonfiction.

sources.title: Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution
sources.annotation: Steven Levy. Where the culture's values came from.

sources.title: The Information: A History, a Theory, a Flood
sources.annotation: James Gleick. From talking drums to Shannon. Beautifully written.

sources.title: The Dream Machine
sources.annotation: Waldrop on Licklider. Free to read on Stripe Press's site.

sources.title: Broad Band: The Untold Story of the Women Who Made the Internet
sources.annotation: Claire L. Evans. The half of the history usually left out.

sources.title: Coders at Work
sources.annotation: Seibel. Fifteen long interviews. Philology, essentially — close reading of practitioners.

sources.title: Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
sources.annotation: Petzold. Builds a computer from a torch and a wire, one patient chapter at a time. The single best bridge from humanities to machine.

sources.title: The Pattern on the Stone
sources.annotation: Danny Hillis. Short, elegant, the whole of computing in 180 pages.

sources.title: The Annotated Turing
sources.annotation: Petzold walks through Turing's 1936 paper line by line. A philologist's book about a mathematician's.

sources.title: Resilient Web Design
sources.annotation: Jeremy Keith. A history of the web's design philosophy. Free, and a two-evening read.

sources.title: A List Apart
sources.annotation: The web's own essay journal since 1998.

sources.title: CSS-Tricks
sources.annotation: Twenty years of CSS problems and their solutions.

sources.title: Josh W. Comeau — essays
sources.annotation: Interactive explanations of CSS and React. Unusually well written.
